title: Before Adopting a Franchise ERP: Connect Inquiry to Store Opening
description: Before adopting a franchise ERP, find where information breaks between consultation, contract and store opening. A 5-stage flow and what to prepare first.
html:
How to connect consultation, contract and store-opening information with a franchise ERP, and the criteria for deciding on adoption.

Why consultation, contract and opening information must connect in one flow

CORE SUMMARY

✔ Evaluating a franchise ERP starts not with comparing feature lists, but with finding where information breaks between consultation and store opening.

✔ When consultation, contract and training information is scattered across individual staff members' memories and files, the same questions come up at every handover.

✔ FDAM connects sales management (prospect consultations and e-franchise agreements) and HQ opening management (documents, interiors and training) in one flow.

✔ Before adoption, organizing your current consultation forms, opening checklists and staff responsibilities first makes the evaluation more efficient.

A franchise ERP is a work management tool built specifically for headquarters, letting HQ record and track franchise sales, store-opening preparation and store operations in one system. Many brands already handle this work with Excel, messaging apps and separate documents, but they often find information breaking down when staff change or the store count grows.

Using store-opening work as the reference point, this post covers what information needs to carry through from consultation to contract and training, and what to check first when evaluating a franchise ERP. The focus is not a list of features but how to design your headquarters workflow.

What goes wrong when information breaks during store opening?

A store opening is rarely handled by one person from start to finish. Typically, the franchise development team handles startup inquiries, legal or sales staff handle contracts, the opening support team handles preparation and training, and the operations team manages the store afterward. The accuracy with which information from each earlier stage is passed on at every handover determines the quality of the opening.

If consultation details live only in someone's personal notes, the contract manager has to re-check which terms the prospective franchisee asked about. If contract progress is tracked in a separate file, the opening support team has to ask again to find out how far the paperwork has come. These breaks happen when there is no structure for passing information along.

The problem is especially pronounced when an opening schedule changes. If the training manager was preparing based on the old schedule, learning of the change late means starting the scheduling over from scratch. With only a few stores, verbal check-ins can get you by, but when openings run in parallel, this approach hits its limits.

This is also the point headquarters evaluating a franchise ERP mention most often. The key to real improvement is a structure in which, even when staff change, the reasoning and progress from earlier stages carry over intact.

A structure where information handoff breaks every time staff change

From consultation to opening: the 5-stage workflow HQ must manage

Viewed in terms of information handoff, store-opening work breaks down into five stages. If you define in advance what information to record at each stage and what the next person needs to check, your work standards become clear whether or not you adopt a system.

First, at the startup inquiry stage, record the inquiry channel, contact information and preferred area. This information becomes the basis for prioritizing consultations. Second, at the consultation stage, record what was discussed, items to verify and the next contact date. When there are several consultations, it is important to record separately what was agreed in earlier sessions and what has yet to be confirmed.

Third, at the contract stage, manage contract progress and related documents. From this point on, the accuracy of records tied to legal procedures matters. Fourth, at the opening preparation and training stage, organize the preparation schedule, training plan and outstanding tasks. Fifth, at the operations handover stage, pass key history and notes up to the opening on to the operations team.

StageInformation to recordWhat the next person checks
Startup inquiryInquiry channel, contact info, preferred areaWho the prospect is and inquiry background
ConsultationDiscussion, items to verify, next contact dateWhat was agreed and what is unconfirmed
ContractContract progress, related documentsConfirmed info needed for opening prep
Opening prep and trainingPrep schedule, training plan, outstanding tasksItems to check before opening
Operations handoverKey history, handover notesFirst visit and early operations support

This table is an example for organizing the workflow. Since every brand has a different organizational structure and process, adjust it to your headquarters' division of responsibilities when applying it. Still, if you review each stage against the question "What does the next person need to know?", it becomes clear which information must be recorded.

Criteria for the information to pass on to the next person at each stage

Franchise sales management: how to connect consultation history and contract information

The recurring problems at the franchise sales stage are breaks in consultation history and difficulty proving when pre-contract disclosure documents were delivered. FDAM provides sales management that runs from registering prospective franchisees through consultation status, sending disclosure documents and e-franchise agreements.

When an inquiry comes in, it is registered as a prospect, and consultation status and history accumulate over time. Even when staff change, the new person checks what was discussed and what remains unconfirmed before continuing the consultation. Consultation progress is organized by staff member, so sales staff juggling several prospects can easily set priorities.

At the contract review stage, disclosure documents are generated and sent via KakaoTalk, email or text. The viewing timestamp is recorded, leaving a history of when the documents were delivered and opened. Under Korea's Franchise Business Act, the delivery date of disclosure documents is important evidence if a dispute arises, so whether this is recorded is worth watching when choosing a franchise ERP.

After signing, the flow connects to e-franchise agreements, and an automatic alert is sent 30 days before a contract expires. This helps reduce problems caused by missed renewal dates. When evaluating a franchise ERP, comparing your current consultation forms and contract management approach against this flow makes for a practical decision.

A structure for checking consultation history and contract status on one screen

HQ opening management: why documents, interiors and training need to be checked together

Once a contract is signed, several people start moving at once. Document preparation, interior work and owner training run in parallel, so if HQ cannot check all three together, outstanding tasks are discovered only right before opening.

Common opening management gaps

When there are only a few openings, staff experience can carry you through, but when openings run in parallel, incomplete documents, delayed construction and unconfirmed training schedules surface only right before opening day.

FDAM's opening management lets HQ check opening readiness through document management, interior management and training management items. Here, headquarters is in charge: HQ reviews the opening progress of multiple stores item by item on one screen.

Document management records the readiness of each document needed for opening. Interior management records construction progress stages to reveal delays. Training management handles training schedules, forms and evaluation results. A structure in which schedule changes are recorded and confirmed by the relevant staff becomes the standard for not missing anything before opening.

This structure is especially effective when staff change. The new person inherits progress as-is from recorded items, not from the previous person's memory. The more openings you have, the more these records matter as a standard for keeping quality consistent even when staff change.

Opening readiness checklist items standardized by HQ

Materials to prepare first when evaluating a franchise ERP

With a franchise ERP, the actual scope of use is determined less by the adoption itself than by the preparation beforehand. Before requesting a consultation, it is efficient to first organize your current consultation forms, opening checklists, staff responsibilities and basic store information.

These materials do not need to be perfectly tidy. In fact, materials that show the current state as-is, meaning where information is scattered, are more useful. If you mark where information gets entered twice and what you have to ask staff about again, you can discuss the scope of adoption concretely.

POINT

General-purpose ERPs are optimized for common functions such as accounting and HR. A franchise-specialized ERP is designed around franchise-specific workflows: franchise sales, store openings and store operations.

To apply the experience HQ accumulates with each opening to the next one, consultation, contract and opening-prep records need to be connected. MS Venter developed FDAM based on its long experience working with franchisor headquarters since its founding in 2007. If you are evaluating adoption, we recommend a consultation to pinpoint which parts of your current workflow would benefit from being connected.

Frequently asked questions

Q1. Which work should we look at first when evaluating a franchise ERP?

Start with the work your staff most often re-check or enter twice. In most cases, information breaks recur in consultation history, contract progress and opening preparation items.

Q2. Does FDAM only support opening management?

No. FDAM supports a continuous workflow: sales management covering startup inquiries, consultations, disclosure documents and e-franchise agreements; opening management covering documents, interiors and training; and operations management covering QSCV inspections and POS sales aggregation.

Q3. Can we confirm the delivery date of disclosure documents in the system?

FDAM sends disclosure documents via KakaoTalk, email or text and records the viewing timestamp, so you can check the history of when they were delivered and opened.

Q4. What should we prepare before adoption for a smooth consultation?

If you organize your existing consultation forms, opening checklists, staff responsibilities and basic store information, we can discuss the scope that fits your headquarters concretely.
